{{Quote|Car'das and Ferasi: this is Syndic Mitth'ras'safis of the Eighth Ruling Family. My brother.|Thrawn, introducing Thrass to his guests|<ref name="OF" />}}
'''Mitth'ras'safis''', also known by his [[Core name/Legends|core name]] '''Thrass''', was a member of the [[Mitth family/Legends|Mitth family]], the Eighth [[Ruling Families/Legends|Ruling Family]] of the [[Chiss Ascendancy/Legends|Chiss Ascendancy]], and was the [[Gender/Legends|brother]] of [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Mitth'raw'nuruodo]], whose core name was Thrawn. Like his brother, Mitth'ras'safis was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] to a [[Mitth'ras'safis's blood family|family]] of commoners but was [[Merit adoptive/Legends|adopted]] into the Eighth ruling family and granted the title of [[Syndic/Legends|Syndic]]. Despite being devoted to his brother, Thrass did not accept all the things that Thrawn did in the name of protecting the [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]], including Thrawn's agenda against the [[Vagaari/Legends|Vagaari]], a [[Species/Legends|species]] of nomadic [[Slavery/Legends|slavers]]. He also saw some of Thrawn's actions as harmful to their family&mdash;even [[Spy/Legends|spying]] on his brother and reporting back to [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Ar'alani/Legends|Ar'alani]] of the [[Chiss Defense Fleet]].

After the [[battle for Outbound Flight]]&mdash;fought between a [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] colony [[Outbound Flight|ship]] carrying an [[Outbound Flight Project|expedition]] attempting to travel beyond [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], a Vagaari war [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]], and Thrawn's [[Picket Force Two]]&mdash;Thrass' and Thrawn's [[Human/Legends|Human]] friend [[Jorj Car'das]] discovered a group of survivors on board while attempting to prevent the [[Starship/Legends|ship]] and its technology from falling into the hands of [[Aristocra/Legends|Aristocra]] [[Chaf'orm'bintrano]] and the [[Chaf family/Legends|Fifth Ruling Family]]. While Car'das stayed behind, Thrass and [[Lorana Jinzler]], the last surviving [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] of the expedition, flew the ''Outbound Flight'' into [[The Redoubt/Legends|the Redoubt]]&mdash;a [[Star cluster/Legends|star cluster]] at the edge of Chiss [[Realspace/Legends|space]]&mdash;to hide it there. Thrass and Jinzler [[Death/Legends|gave their lives]] to protect the remaining passengers of the ''Outbound Flight'' when they crash-landed the ship on one of the small [[Planetoid/Legends|planetoids]] in the cluster. About [[22 ABY/Legends|fifty years later]], his remains were discovered by [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and his [[Marriage/Legends|wife]] [[Mara Jade Skywalker]], when they [[Expedition to Outbound Flight|visited]] the [[Outbound Flight Colony|colony]] created by the Outbound Flight [[Survivors (Outbound Flight)|survivors]] and their [[Colonists|offspring]].

==Biography==
===Early life===
{{Quote|We were both born as commoners. I can live that way again if I have to. But I'll do what I can to assure that the Eighth Family doesn't release or rematch you on my account.''"<br />"''I'm not worried about my own position. I'm trying to keep my brother from throwing away a fine and honorable career for nothing.|Thrawn and Thrass|<ref name="OF" />}}
[[File:Outboundthrawn.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Thrass' brother, Force Commander Mitth'raw'nuruodo of the Chiss Expansionary Fleet]]
The [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] Mitth'ras'safis and his [[Gender/Legends|brother]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Mitth'raw'nuruodo]], who were known by their [[Core name/Legends|core names]] "Thrass" and "Thrawn," respectively, were [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] to a [[Mitth'ras'safis's blood family|family]] of commoners in the [[Chiss Ascendancy/Legends|Chiss Ascendancy]], living their early [[Standard year/Legends|years]] as simple members of Chiss society. When they were of age, they were both deemed worthy to become [[Merit adoptive/Legends|merit adoptives]] in the [[Mitth family/Legends|Mitth family]], which was the eighth among the nine [[Ruling Families/Legends|Ruling Families]] that formed the Chiss government of the [[Time/Legends|time]]. While Thrawn was a clever military strategist and quickly gained rank among the [[Chiss Expansionary Fleet/Legends|Chiss Expansionary Fleet]]&mdash;becoming the youngest to reach the rank of [[Force Commander]] before [[27 BBY/Legends|27 BBY]]&mdash;Thrass chose a [[Politics/Legends|political]] career, holding the status of [[Syndic/Legends|Syndic]] around the same time.<ref name="OF" />

Thrass was deeply devoted to his brother and watched with worry when Thrawn took what Thrass saw as unnecessary risks by engaging enemies who had not acted directly against the Ascendancy. Because Chiss had [[Defensive-only doctrine|strict rules]] concerning preemptive strikes against potential enemies, some of Thrawn's more aggressive actions were deemed unethical by the Chiss [[Defense Hierarchy]]. When Thrawn had been given command of the [[Crustai asteroid base|Crustai base]], he was involved in [[Skirmish in the Crustai system|action]] against [[Vagaari/Legends|Vagaari]] moving around the same area. The Vagaari were a nomadic [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Alien/Legends|aliens]] who captured [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]] from one [[Planet/Legends|planet]] and then moved on to another location, without having a [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of their own. The aliens had been moving near the borders of the Ascendancy, attacking low-technology planets, but had not made any moves against the Chiss. Thrass saw that Thrawn's active role in the matter was threatening the status that the [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] held in the military, as those who violated the Non-Aggression Law could be condemned into [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exile]].<ref name="OF" />

===Encounter with Humans===
{{Dialogue|Thrawn|You could try Minnisiat. They speak that better than they do Cheunh. Or you could use Sy Bisti, which I believe you also know.|Thrass|Yes. If that would be easier.|Car'das|Actually, we'd prefer you stick with Cheunh, if you don't mind. We could use the practice.|Thrass|That you could. And since you were both instrumental in saving my brother's life&hellip;I suppose it would be all right for you to call me Thrass.|attr=Mitth'ras'safis, Mitth'raw'nuruodo, and Jorj Car'das|src=<ref name="OF" />}}
[[File:Jorj.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Thrawn's human friend, Jorj Car'das]]
Around the same time as the Chiss' first encounters with the Vagaari, Thrawn also crossed paths with two [[Starship/Legends|ships]] from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]: the small-time [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] vessel ''[[Bargain Hunter]]''&mdash;crewed by three [[Human/Legends|Humans]] named [[Dubrak Qennto]], [[Maris Ferasi]], and [[Jorj Car'das]]&mdash;and a [[Progga's starship|ship]] belonging to a [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] named [[Progga]], who had been [[Skirmish between Progga and the Bargain Hunter|following]] them into the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]]. After [[Skirmish between Progga and Picket Force Two|destroying]] Progga's ship, Thrawn captured the Humans and brought them to his [[Unidentified asteroid (Crustai system)|asteroid]] base in the [[Crustai system/Legends|Crustai system]]. Thrass and [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Ar'alani/Legends|Ar'alani]], one of Thrawn's superiors in the Expansionary Defense Force, learned about the presence of the Humans and Thrawn's most recent activities against the Vagaari from [[Aristocra/Legends|Aristocra]] [[Chaf'orm'bintrano]], a high-ranking member of the [[Chaf family/Legends|Chaf family]] who had visited the base to meet with Thrawn concerning interests that the family had in the [[Star system/Legends|system]].<ref name="OF" />

Soon after Chaf'orm'bintrano's visit, Thrass and Ar'alani arrived at the Crustai base and found the Humans still living there and moving more or less freely around. Qennto, the captain of the captured ''Bargain Hunter'', and Ferasi, his girlfriend and second-in-command, were still accompanied by guards whenever they went outside their quarters, but Car'das was allowed to come and go as he pleased. Thrawn had also given Qennto access to the treasure he had found aboard the [[Vagaari plunder ship|Vagaari vessel]] that he had captured&mdash;Qennto had traveled a lot and seen many cultures, and was thus knowledgeable about different species of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Yet such a liberty did not sit well with Ar'alani and Thrass. Thrawn used this as a distraction and slipped away with Car'das and Ferasi to investigate another ongoing [[Battle of Geroon|Vagaari attack]] in a nearby system. During the battle, Thrawn's [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], the ''[[Springhawk/Legends|Springhawk]]'', suffered damage to its [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]], and the Commander was wounded and would have [[Death/Legends|died]] if his Human companions had not helped him. After their return to Thrawn's base of operations, Thrass thanked the duo for saving his brother's life, even allowing them to call him by his core name, a privilege usually only granted for friends or other socially equal people. Thrass also openly expressed his worry for Thrawn's action despite the Humans being present and reprimanded his brother for what he had done in front of them.<ref name="OF" />

Despite Thrass' warning, Thrawn soon went out with Car'das to investigate another group of unidentified vessels. They discovered that it was [[Special Task Force One]] of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], led by [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] [[Vicelord]] [[Siv Kav]] and Commander [[Kinman Doriana/Legends|Stratis]]&mdash;Stratis was a false name used by Kinman Doriana, an [[Agent/Legends|agent]] for both [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] of the Republic and his alter-ego, the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Sidious&mdash;which had been sent out to intercept and destroy the Republic [[Outbound Flight Project|expedition]] traveling aboard a large [[Colony ship/Legends|colony ship]] named ''[[Outbound Flight]]''. Thrawn [[Destruction of Special Task Force One|disposed]] of the task force without suffering any losses of his own, capturing its leaders and learning from them that the expedition that Kav and Stratis wanted to destroy was approaching Chiss territory. Stratis warned Thrawn about the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] traveling aboard the ship, claiming they would wish to put the Chiss under their rule, and did his best to persuade the Commander to destroy it. With his own strike force decimated, Stratis was unable to complete the mission that Sidious had given him if Thrawn refused to destroy the ''Outbound Flight'' in his stead. After Thrawn's return to his [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] base, Thrass learned about his brother's latest act of aggression and believed that the Chiss had suffered losses in the battle. In truth, Thrawn had left the ''Springhawk''{{'s}} sister [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser]], the [[Whirlwind (Chiss)/Legends|''Whirlwind'']]&mdash;which had been equipped with a [[Gravity well projector/Legends|Vagaari ship net]] that he had earlier acquired&mdash;to stand guard over the captured [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|Trade Federation vessel]]. Again seeing that Chiss lives had been lost, Thrass saw no other choice but to contact Ar'alani and ask her to investigate Thrawn's actions. The Admiral returned to the Crustai base promptly and started to look into Thrawn's activities and interview his personnel.<ref name="OF" />

===Destruction of the ''Outbound Flight''===
{{Quote|My brother cares deeply about his blood family, including me. But he's disturbed by what he sees as my self-destructive behavior&hellip;and as a syndic of the Eighth Ruling Family, his duty is to protect that family's honor and position.''"<br />"''So he calls an ''admiral'' down on you?|Thrawn and Car'das, after Thrass calls Admiral Ar'alani back to Crustai|<ref name="OF" />}}
[[File:Outboundship.jpg|thumb|left|250px|''Outbound Flight'']]
Thrass accompanied Ar'alani and their reluctant guide, Car'das, to the scene of the battle, where Thrawn had destroyed the Trade Federation task force. While Ar'alani and her [[Ar'alani's inspection group|inspection group]] conducted their investigations, Thrawn spent the time on board the only remaining Trade Federation [[Darkvenge|ship]], speaking with Doriana and learning more about their mission and Outbound Flight; he used Ar'alani's orders to patrol the area as an excuse to stay away from his base. Car'das tried to convince Thrass and Ar'alani that Thrawn's actions against the Trade Federation were justified, but was worried about what would happen to him and his companions if the Admiral chose to bring up charges against the Commander. Three [[Standard day/Legends|days]] after their trip to the battle site, Thrass witnessed a confrontation between Car'das and Ar'alani when the Admiral claimed that the Human was a [[Spy/Legends|spy]] and ordered him detained into his quarters. Desperate to escape the Chiss base, Car'das stole a long-range [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]]&mdash;unaware that Thrawn had specially prepared it for him just for that purpose&mdash;and escaped to seek help from the Vagaari. Thrawn had been able to anticipate Car'das' action and used it to lure the Vagaari into the same trap that he had been preparing for the ''Outbound Flight''.<ref name="OF" />

The Jedi of the ''Outbound Flight'' refused to return to the Galactic Republic as Thrawn demanded. When Thrawn's stolen [[Gravity well projector/Legends|gravity well projector]] pulled the Vagaari into his trap, the aliens ordered the exploration team to surrender to them. The shuttle that Car'das had stolen from the Crustai base had carried several [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] and [[Droideka/Legends|droidekas]], and having learned about the existence of fighting machines, the Vagaari were eager to get more. Car'das convinced them that Thrawn's base had more of them, but when the Vagaari saw the huge colony ship from the Republic, he assured them that it carried even more [[Droid/Legends|droids]]. The [[Battle for Outbound Flight|three-way battle]] that ensued between the Vagaari, the ''Outbound Flight'', and Thrawn's [[Troop/Legends|troops]] finally ended when [[Vulture-class starfighter/Legends|droid starfighters]]&mdash;taken from the Trade Federation ship and specially modified by Thrawn's people to carry [[radiation bomb]]s&mdash;rammed each of the six [[Dreadnaught-class heavy cruiser/Legends|''Dreadnaught''-class cruisers]] forming the large colony ship. The [[Radiation/Legends|radiation]] being discharged from the bombs killed every living being on board the six cruisers, but left the [[Central Storage Core|storage core]] intact, as no one was expected to be there.<ref name="OF" />

Several [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]] after the battle, Thrass and Ar'alani arrived on the scene, the former mostly concentrating on helping the [[Geroon (species)|Geroons]] who had been rescued from the Vagaari [[Warship/Legends|warships]], where they had been used as living shields, while the Admiral accompanied Thrawn to investigate the ''Outbound Flight''. On board the rescue vessel, Thrass met Car'das, who had been rescued with the Geroons, and the two spoke about the ways that Thrawn had been using them as part of his plan to remove the Vagaari threat. Thrass was slightly insulted by the fact that he had been used as a pawn, but Car'das understood Thrawn's reasoning in the matter and did not mind the role that the Commander had given him. After hearing that Aristocra Chaf'orm'bintrano was on his way to investigate the events and arrest Thrawn for overstepping his mandate as Force Commander, Thrass went to warn his brother about the approaching trouble.<ref name="OF" />

Thrass and Car'das found Thrawn and Ar'alani on ''[[Dreadnaught-One]]'', the [[Command ship/Legends|commanding vessel]] of the ''Outbound Flight''. Learning about the Aristocra's intentions, Thrawn and Ar'alani made a plan to move the vessel to the [[Pesfavri/Legends|nearest Defense Fleet base]], but Chaf'orm'bintrano arrived before they had time to leave. Thrawn warned that having the ''Outbound Flight'' falling into the hands of any one family would upset the balance of powers in the Chiss Ascendancy, and it would thus be better to destroy the entire ship if it was the only way to prevent that from happening. The Aristocra contacted Ar'alani, ordering her to put Thrawn under detention. The Admiral's station in the Defense Hierarchy did not allow her to ignore a direct order from a member of a ruling family, and she was duty-bound to arrest the Commander. While Ar'alani, Thrawn, and the Chiss team who had been accompanying them left the ''Outbound Flight'', Thrass and Car'das stayed on board in order to put the ship on [[Autopilot/Legends|autopilot]] and send it on a one-way trip into the local [[Star/Legends|star]].<ref name="OF" />

===Death===
{{Quote|Your people will come here someday. Until then, they have enough food and supplies to last for generations. They'll survive. I know they will.''"<br />"''Then let us prepare for the end. I've known you and your people only briefly, Jedi Lorana Jinzler. But in that time, I've learned to admire and respect you. I hope that someday humans and Chiss will be able to work side by side in peace.''"<br />"''As do I, Syndic Mitth'ras'safis of the Eighth Ruling Family.|Lorana Jinzler and Thrass, moments before their death|<ref name="OF" />}}
[[File:Lorana.jpg|thumb|right|243px|Jedi Lorana Jinzler died together with Thrass.]]
When Thrass and Car'das were almost ready to set the autopilot and leave, [[Lorana Jinzler]], a [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] who had been among the passengers of the expedition, arrived on the bridge and revealed that there were still nearly sixty people on board&mdash;they had survived the radiation bombs in the storage core, where they had been ordered by the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] leading the expedition, [[Jorus C'baoth]]. The shuttle that Thrass and Car'das had used was too small to safely extract all of them from the ship in time, but Jinzler was convinced that she could [[Pilot/Legends|fly]] the ''Outbound Flight'' by herself through her control of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. Thrass was able to provide them with the information about a safe location inside a [[Star cluster/Legends|star cluster]] known to Chiss as [[The Redoubt/Legends|the Redoubt]], where they could stay out of sight while Thrass would return to negotiate with the [[Council of Families]] about ''Outbound Flight''{{'s}} return to the Republic. Following Jinzler's order, Car'das stayed behind while Thrass and the Jedi took the ship to its final voyage into the star cluster.<ref name="OF" />

Because of the serious damage that the ''Outbound Flight'' had suffered in the fight, it was taxing to Jinzler to operate the ship alone, and Thrass found no way to contact the remaining crew members, who had been left into the storage core. Even with all possible speed, the trip into the Redoubt took several hours. When the [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] stopped working, Thrass and Jinzler had to search the system to find a suitable planet for them to leave the ship in [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] while the negotiations with the Chiss would be conducted. They found a small [[Planetoid/Legends|planetoid]] in the system, but setting a large vehicle like the ''Outbound Flight'' on an orbit when its drive systems were damaged turned out to be impossible. Thrass employed what was left of the [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] systems to find a valley, filled with small stones, which was located along their route and where the impact with the planetoid's surface would be less violent.<ref name="OF" />

====Saving the survivors====
{{Quote|You can't handle the landing alone, [&hellip;] But I could do that while you go. [&hellip;]''"<br />"''And who would keep the remaining systems from self-destroying while you cleared a path through the pylons for me? [&hellip;] No, Jedi Jinzler. It appears we will both be giving our lives for your people.|Lorana Jinzler and Mitth'ras'safis|<ref name="OF" />}}
The only other [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]-capable vehicle on board was a [[Delta-12 Skysprite-class|Delta-12 ''Skysprite'']] that had been stored on ''[[Dreadnaught-Three]]''. The small, two-person ship had been meant to be used by [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and his Master [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], who accompanied the expedition during its first trip around known space but had been pulled out prematurely by Supreme Chancellor Palpatine, who had not wanted Skywalker to die in Doriana's ambush. Thrass and Jinzler planned to use the ''Skysprite'' to return to Chiss space and negotiate for the relocation of the survivors of the ''Outbound Flight''. To have easy access to the two-person ship, they planned to land the ''Outbound Flight'' in a way that would place ''[[Dreadnaught-Six]]'' at the bottom and leave number three on top. They were forced to rethink their plan when they learned that the survivors had moved away from the storage core and were on ''[[Dreadnaught-Four]]'' instead&mdash;which was directly opposite ''Dreadnaught-One'' where Thrass and Jinzler were.<ref name="OF" />

To protect the survivors, Thrass and Jinzler knew that they would have to put ''Dreadnaught-Four'' as far away from the impact as they could. Having their own ship hit first would cost them their own lives, but neither Thrass nor Jinzler hesitated to make the sacrifice. While Thrass had been suspicious of Humans when he first encountered them, through Car'das and Jinzler he had learned to appreciate them. In the moments before their death, he voiced this newfound appreciation to Jinzler, sharing with her the hope that their two peoples would one day be able to work together peacefully. Their thoughts also lingered on the people for whom they would be giving their lives before the ''Outbound Flight'' slammed into the planetoid, killing Thrass and the young Jedi.<ref name="OF" />

===Legacy===
{{Quote|It's ''Outbound Flight'', ''[&hellip;]'' We're not alone, Aristocra Formbi. There are survivors aboard.|Luke Skywalker to Aristocra Chaf'orm'bintrano|<ref name="Quest">''[[Survivor's Quest]]''</ref>}}
The final fate of Thrass and the ''Outbound Flight'' remained a mystery until [[22 ABY/Legends|22 ABY]], when a Chiss [[Unidentified Chiss patrol|patrol]] located the ship's remains inside the Redoubt. Chaf'orm'bintrano assembled a [[Expedition to Outbound Flight|larger team]] and also invited two Jedi from the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] to join the expedition, Jedi Master [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and his [[Marriage/Legends|wife]], [[Mara Jade Skywalker]]. The sacrifice of Thrass and Jinzler had paid off, and the [[Survivors (Outbound Flight)|survivors]] of the ''Outbound Flight'' had built a [[Outbound Flight Colony|colony]] in the remains of the ships with their [[Colonists|offspring]]. The survivors believed that the Jedi had been to blame for the destruction of the ''Outbound Flight'', and they were distrustful toward Skywalker and his wife, locking them inside a [[Turbolift/Legends|turbolift]] car. After escaping from the trap, the duo made their way down to what was left of ''Dreadnaught-One'' and found the remains of two people on the bridge, where they had laid undisturbed for fifty years. The bridge had been badly damaged during the crash and, because of the way ''Outbound Flight'' had been constructed, it was upside down and the skeletons were resting on what had once been the ceiling. The presence of a [[Charric pistol|charric]], a Chiss weapon, revealed that one of the bodies belonged to one of the [[Color/Legends|blue]]-skinned aliens&mdash;though the Skywalkers were unaware of the fallen Chiss's identity, it was Thrass. [[Lorana Jinzler's lightsaber|Lorana's lightsaber]] was recognized by her brother, [[Dean Jinzler|Dean]], who was among the expedition, and helped to identify the other body.<ref name="Quest" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|You're gifted in many ways, my brother. But you have yet to develop the farsightedness you will need to survive the intrigues and conflicts of political life.|Mitth'raw'nuruodo|<ref name="OF" />}}
Thrass was devoted to both his [[Blood/Legends|blood]] family&mdash;including his brother Thrawn&mdash;and his adopted family, which made him feel conflicted about his loyalties. He was worried about Thrawn's actions, which he saw as a risk to his brother's career as well as to Thrawn's relationship with the Eighth Ruling Family. He was drawn between his loyalty to Thrawn and his loyalty to what he perceived to be the good of the family, as he strictly believed in the non-aggression laws of the Chiss Ascendancy. While he respected his brother's abilities as a tactician, Thrass often found himself unable to understand his reasoning and plans, and also found it insulting that his brother would use him as a pawn in his plan to lure the Vagaari into an aggressive strike against the Ascendancy.<ref name="OF" />

Unlike his brother's military pursuits, Thrass was interested in politics. However, Thrawn believed that Thrass was still lacking in the farsightedness that he would need to excel in such a career. As a merit adoptive member of a Ruling Family&mdash;who, just like his brother, had the possibility to become a more permanent [[Trial-born/Legends|Trial-born]] member&mdash;Thrass wore gray clothes with highlights colored burgundy, the color of the Mitth family. He had the blue skin, blue-black hair, and red, glowing eyes which were typical of Chiss. In addition to the Chiss language, [[Cheunh/Legends|Cheunh]], Thrass spoke fluent [[Minnisiat/Legends|Minnisiat]] and accented [[Sy Bisti/Legends|Sy Bisti]]. He carried a small, hand-held [[Mitth'ras'safis's charric|charric]] as a personal weapon.<ref name="OF" />

Despite his initial suspicion and dislike toward Humans, Thrass learned to admire and respect Jorj Car'das and his people&mdash;he even revealed his thoughts and worries about his brother's actions to the man. In addition, he soon learned to respect Jedi Lorana Jinzler, when the two of them flew the badly damaged ''Outbound Flight'' into the Redoubt, sharing with her the hopes that Chiss and Humans could find a way to live together in peace in times to come. When Thrass learned that he and Jinzler would be trading their lives for those of the survivors, he did not hesitate to make the sacrifice, but would have liked to save Jinzler as well.<ref name="OF" />

==Equipment==
{{Quote|And, Exhibit Two.''"<br />"''Is that what I think it is?''"<br />"''I think so. It's a few decades out of date, but the style is unmistakable. It's a Chiss charric.|Luke Skywalker and Mara Jade Skywalker, upon finding Thrass's charric in the remains of the Outbound Flight|<ref name="Quest" />}}
When traveling with Ar'alani to Thrawn's Crustai base, Thrass wore a short<ref name="OF" /> yellow and gray<ref name="Edelweiss Outbound">{{PenguinRandomHouse|url=books/195403/outbound-flight-star-wars-legends-by-timothy-zahn/9780345456847|text=Outbound Flight: Star Wars Legends}}</ref> [[Chiss robes of state|robe]] and tall boots. His outfit was a patchwork of grey and burgundy. Concealed in his tunic, he carried a small hand weapon,<ref name="OF" /> a charric adorned with [[Written Cheunh|Chiss lettering]],<ref name="Quest" /> when he boarded the ''Outbound Flight'' with Car'das.<ref name="OF" /> Fifty years later his weapon was recovered by Luke Skywalker and Mara Jade Skywalker.<ref name="Quest" />

==Behind the scenes==
Mitth'ras'safis made his first appearance in [[Timothy Zahn]]'s novel ''[[Survivor's Quest]]'' in [[2004]] as an unidentified Chiss [[Skeleton/Legends|skeleton]] discovered on the bridge of the ''Outbound Flight''.<ref name="Quest" /> Zahn expanded his background&mdash;revealing his name and connection to Thrawn&mdash;in his later novel, [[Outbound Flight (novel)|''Outbound Flight'']], in [[2006]].<ref name="OF" /> He was first pictured on the [[:File:Outbound Flight Essential Legends Edition cover.jpg|cover art]] for the ''[[The Essential Legends Collection]]'' reprint of ''Outbound Flight'', which was published on [[August 15]], [[2023]]. The picture depicted Thrass with the yellow color<ref name="Edelweiss Outbound" /> of the Chaf family instead of the patchwork of gray and burgundy color of the Mitth family he wore in the novel.<ref name="OF" />
